text:
maria: FYI we started getting a flurry of OOM alerts in us-west-2 around 03:12 UTC after the model-serving push. stack traces show allocator pressure + kernel fallback oscillation. attaching a perf snapshot: https://perf.internal/reports/2865432123

sam: grabbing the profile now. quick read: kernel-selector is flipping from the quantized matmul -> native fp32 for batches > 12. autotuner metrics show a recent regression in kernel score because latency variance spiked. seems to increase workspace demand.

cheng: also seeing KV cache churn — TTLs dropped to 15s during the surge (some tenant configs changed). that forced more cold KV priming which increases peak workspace allocations.

elaine: suggested immediate mitigation (short playbook):
1) throttle prefetch: set prefetch_ratio=0.25 for us-west-2 runtime nodes
2) enforce small-batch cap: max_effective_batch=8 for the affected model route
3) pin kernel selector policy to prefer quantized kernels for seq_len>512
4) bump KV TTL to 120s for heavy-traffic tenants (temporary)
5) enable allocator soft-slab-reclaim (decrease slab_size from 256MB->128MB)
6) circuit-breaker: reject requests > 600k tokens or that declare long_history=true with 503 fallback

maria: +1 to that ordering. priority is to stop OOMs before rolling new perf fixes. which of these can be live patched with minimal deploy?

sam: I can live-patch prefetch + batch cap via feature flags. kernel selector pin needs a config toggle on the controller, low-risk. allocator slab change needs node config reload (no full deploy). KV TTL change is service-level, safe to change.

max: prepping the hotfix for allocator: patch config map runtime-allocator -> {"slab_size_mb": "128", "soft_reclaim_pct": "15"}. will apply to a subset of nodes first (canary pool id=usw2-canary).

oz: I'm on KV TTL. running:
```
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/kv/config -d '{"route":"/model/*","ttl_s":120}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
Will monitor hit rate and eviction slope.

sam: feature flag toggles:
```
redwood feature set runtime.prefetch_ratio=0.25 --env=us-west-2
redwood feature set runtime.max_effective_batch=8 --route=model/reasoner --env=us-west-2
redwood config set kernel_selector.policy="prefer_quant_for_long_seq" --env=us-west-2
```
Applying now to canaries.

infra-bot: rollback-trigger: detected 4 OOMs in last 90s on node-runtime-54. automatic rollback to v2.14.0 queued.

deploy-bot: rollback started: v2.14.1 -> v2.14.0 (initiated by infra-bot)

elaine: good call. while rollback happens, we should also enable the circuit breaker rule. I'll add a rule: 503 for token_count>600k + metric tag "oom-risk" to route to redwood-tiny-quant fallback.

maria: can someone post the exact breaker rule? will add to runbook.

elaine: breaker rule snippet:
```
breaker.add_rule({
  "route_match": "/model/reasoner",
  "condition": "token_count > 600000 || long_history == true",
  "action": "respond_with_fallback",
  "fallback_model": "redwood-tiny-quant",
  "response_code": 503,
  "tag": "oom-risk"
})
```
Applied to us-west-2 traffic tier.

cheng: monitor notes: after the prefetch + batch cap we should see average workspace per-request drop ~20-30% in synthetic tests because we avoid long contiguous allocations. also check KV cold-start rate — that should drop after TTL bump.

sam: canaries are green for prefetch+batch cap now. kernel pin looks good on canary nodes; quantized kernels for seq_len>512 are serving with slightly higher lat but stable memory footprint.

max: allocator canary applied to 10 nodes. initial telemetry: max resident dropped ~18% on canaries. no regressions yet.

oz: KV TTL change propagated; cold-starts down 65% on affected routes. eviction pressure reduced.

deploy-bot: rollback complete: v2.14.0 active in us-west-2 (2026-03-18T03:26:30Z).

maria: summary for runbook entry: immediate actions taken: rollback deploy -> enable prefetch throttle -> limit effective batch -> pin kernel policy -> bump KV TTL -> apply allocator soft-slab config -> add circuit breaker w/ fallback. all canaries look stable.

elaine: follow-ups:
- run a 4h soak on us-west-2 with traffic replay
- add a unit/regression test that ensures kernel-autotuner won't prefer high-variance kernel under noisy latency (blocker)
- add end-to-end test for large-history requests to validate breaker triggers and fallback correctness
- add a perf alert for kernel-selection flips (quantized->fp32) with count threshold 3 in 5m

maria: thanks. I'll update the incident board and assign a retro. tagging @cheng @sam @max for post-mortem items. :eyes:

sam: logging repro job + attaching flamegraphs to the incident ticket: https://perf.internal/trace/2865432123/flame

maria: closing this thread — keep monitoring and post if OOMs recur.

infra-bot: monitoring: all OOM alerts cleared for us-west-2 (last 15m). :white_check_mark:
